name: Negative ablations and counterexamples - where distractor handling, memory or an online target model do not help
bibliography: (1) Peize Sun, Jinkun Cao, Yi Jiang, Zehuan Yuan, Song Bai, Kris Kitani, Ping Luo. DanceTrack: Multi-Object Tracking in Uniform Appearance and Diverse Motion. arXiv:2111.14690 (v3, 24 May 2022); published at CVPR 2022 [uncertain: the arXiv page lists no venue]; code/data https://github.com/DanceTrack/DanceTrack. (2) Cheng-Yen Yang, Hsiang-Wei Huang, Wenhao Chai, Zhongyu Jiang, Jenq-Neng Hwang. SAMURAI: Adapting Segment Anything Model for Zero-Shot Visual Tracking with Motion-Aware Memory. arXiv:2411.11922 v2 (preprint); https://arxiv.org/html/2411.11922v2 ; code https://github.com/yangchris11/samurai. (3) Voigtlaender et al. Siam R-CNN, CVPR 2020, arXiv:1911.12836 (counterexample from its own Tables 3/7/8; full record in N02). (4) Mayer et al. KeepTrack, ICCV 2021, arXiv:2103.16556 (own Tables 1, 10, 11, Fig. 7; full record in N01). (5) Project's own negative cards (internal, not literature): z13_candidate_identity_v1, z13_candidate_ranker_v1, z13_observed_memory_v1, z13_query_memory_v1, z13_absolute_confidence_v1 in E:/Dissertation/experiments/project_history.json. Duplicates: none beyond preprint/conference pairs noted.
full_text_checked: DanceTrack: full PDF v3 text extracted (Sec. 3 statistics, Table 2 oracle association, Tables 4-6); SAMURAI: full HTML v2 (Tables 3-5, attribute table, method text); Siam R-CNN and KeepTrack: full HTML as in N01/N02. Not done: a systematic search of 2023-2026 negative ablations (left to N14/N16), STMTrack/KYS/LTMU/STARK ablations (covered by N05/N06/N08/N09).
task_and_output: Screening across sources: MOT on DanceTrack (boxes + ids, HOTA/AssA/IDF1); SOT with SAM2-based memory (box/mask, AUC); SOT re-detection (Siam R-CNN) and candidate association (KeepTrack) - box per frame with success AUC/EAO.
data_and_independent_videos: DanceTrack: 100 videos (40 train / 25 val / 35 test), uniform-appearance group dancing, numbers here on val with YOLOX detections or GT boxes. SAMURAI: LaSOT test (280), LaSOText (150), GOT-10k test; zero-shot (no training). Siam R-CNN/KeepTrack: standard SOT test sets (see N01/N02). Project: train26 (reused), dev35.
target_size_and_input_resolution: Not applicable for a screening across sources (each source as in its own record: DanceTrack full-HD video frames with YOLOX input; SAMURAI SAM2 1024 px input; KeepTrack 480 px crop; Siam R-CNN full frame).
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: DanceTrack 20 fps, mostly static/slow camera, strong non-linear object motion and frequent position switches; SOT benchmarks 25-30 fps with camera motion.
detector_and_exemplar: DanceTrack: YOLOX detector trained on DanceTrack train, or GT boxes for the oracle study; SAMURAI: no detector, first-frame box prompt; Siam R-CNN: re-detection with Faster R-CNN; KeepTrack: no detector.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: Not applicable for the screening (DanceTrack baselines are off-the-shelf trackers; SAMURAI is training-free on top of SAM2.1; Siam R-CNN/KeepTrack see N02/N01).
controls_seeds_splits: DanceTrack: same detections/GT boxes, association method varied (IoU only, + Kalman, + appearance; SORT vs DeepSORT vs BYTE vs OC-SORT). SAMURAI: module on/off (motion, memory selection) and Kalman weight sweep on LaSOT, single runs. Siam R-CNN: Argmax/short-term/long-term variants. KeepTrack: 0 vs 2 vs 9 GNN layers. No seeds or confidence intervals in any of these sources.
metrics_and_numbers: Counterexamples with location: (a) DanceTrack Table 4 (val, YOLOX dets): SORT HOTA 47.8 / AssA 31.0 / IDF1 48.3 vs DeepSORT (SORT + appearance matching) 45.8 / 29.7 / 46.8 - adding appearance lowered every metric; authors: DeepSORT shows 'worse performance instead'. Table 2 (GT boxes, oracle association): on DanceTrack the best association is IoU-only; adding a linear motion model or appearance does not help, and 'when using appearance similarity, all metrics are worse than not using any appearance cue' (Sec. 4). Table 5: IoU-only HOTA 44.7 vs Kalman 47.8 vs LSTM 51.6 (motion helps). (b) SAMURAI Table 4 (LaSOT AUC vs Kalman weight): 0.00 72.67; 0.15 74.23; 0.25 73.76; 0.50 72.92 (Pnorm 80.49 < 80.67 without motion) - motion-based re-scoring helps only in a narrow weight range; Table 3: memory selection alone +4.35 AUC (68.32 -> 72.67), motion alone +2.49; but on LaSOText illumination variation SAMURAI-B 67.3 vs SAM2.1-B 69.5 and SAMURAI-L 69.0 vs 71.4 - the motion/memory gate hurts under illumination change. SAM2's own predicted-IoU/affinity is described as 'not a very robust indicator' among similar objects. (c) Siam R-CNN: long-term re-detection + TDPA under the VOT2018 reset protocol EAO 0.140 vs 0.408 for the short-term (previous-box-centred) variant (Tables 3/8); conversely the short-term variant collapses on LaSOT (55.7 vs 64.8 AUC, Table 7). (d) KeepTrack: removing the learned GNN costs only 0.5 LaSOT AUC (66.6 vs 67.1, Table 11); gains on OTB-100 only +0.8 AUC; authors note distractors crossing the target are very hard since position is then of limited use (Fig. 7). (e) Project (internal): candidate identity propagation C -3.29 p.p. [-5.91; -0.89] vs top1 (runs/z13_candidate_identity_20261021/report.json); observation memory C -0.127 p.p. [-5.08; +3.45] vs single exemplar (runs/z13_observed_memory_20261021/report.json); query memory C +0.000 vs last (runs/z13_query_memory_20261021/report.json).
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: yes for all literature sources (val/test splits). Target absence: SAMURAI/Siam R-CNN/KeepTrack yes via long-term sets; DanceTrack not applicable (MOT). Similar distractors: yes - DanceTrack is built for uniform appearance (re-ID cosine distance between co-existing people lower than MOT17, Fig. 3a); SAMURAI targets crowded similar objects. Occlusion: yes (DanceTrack frequent occlusion/position switches; LaSOT attributes). Night/low light: only as LaSOText illumination-variation attribute in SAMURAI (negative effect); otherwise not reported. Sequential operation on own predictions: yes in all trackers.
mechanism_summary: Common pattern of the counterexamples: (1) appearance-based identity cues hurt when co-existing objects look alike (DanceTrack: adding appearance to SORT lowers HOTA/AssA/IDF1; with oracle boxes IoU-only is best); (2) a confidence/quality signal produced by the same model is misleading among similar objects (SAM2 affinity/IoU), and a corrective gate (Kalman re-scoring, memory selection) helps only in a narrow parameter range and can hurt under illumination change; (3) global re-detection with sequence selection is harmful when the target mostly stays near its previous position and is reset on failure (Siam R-CNN VOT2018), while local-only search fails on long disappearances (LaSOT) - the right choice depends on the episode type; (4) learned association layers add little over a good candidate encoding (KeepTrack 0-GNN). No published proposed modification here; implication only.
transfer_limits: Our setting is closest to DanceTrack's regime: same-class neighbours (cars/pedestrians in BDD100K MOT) with weak appearance (721 grey hexals, 34 motion/brightness types, no colour/texture), short loss episodes (<= 30 frames at 30 Hz), a small moving crop (~2x target) and a correction that is consumed by ByteTrack/MASA association. DanceTrack's message (appearance hurts, motion helps) suggests FlyVis identity cues may behave like weak appearance - consistent with our candidate identity result. SAMURAI's illumination-variation drop is relevant to the low-light/over-exposure conditions of the dissertation. Siam R-CNN's VOT2018 contrast warns that a re-detection/selection module should be gated by episode type (short loss near prediction vs long absence). Limits: DanceTrack is people with GT-quality detections and 20 fps; SAMURAI uses SAM2 RGB features; none of the sources test 34-type motion features.
research_questions_addressed: 5.1 (caution, direct evidence): the maximum of a quality/affinity score is not evidence of the right object among similar ones (SAMURAI on SAM2; KeepTrack history-max rule exists for that reason). 5.2 (caution): appearance-based memory/identity is weak among uniform-appearance objects (DanceTrack); memory gates can hurt under illumination change (SAMURAI). 5.3: not addressed. 5.4 (direct evidence): motion and IoU cues dominate association when appearance is uniform - so a no-fly motion/IoU guard is a strong control and may capture most of the benefit.
candidate_node_change: Not applicable as a new node change (screening of counterexamples). Implications for the chosen change: any FlyVis identity/readout change must be compared against (i) IoU-only and Kalman-gated corrections, (ii) the same mechanism on eye input R1, and (iii) a variant without appearance (geometry/score only); add an explicit stop if the FlyVis variant does not beat the geometry-only variant (DanceTrack pattern) and report results separately for low-light / over-exposed videos (SAMURAI IV pattern).
strongest_objection: Counterexamples come from different regimes (people dancing at 20 fps, SAM2 masks, full-frame SOT); they show conditions where mechanisms fail, not that they will fail for FlyVis. Negative ablations are under-reported in the literature, so this screening is biased toward positive-leaning papers' own side remarks; it cannot establish absence of benefit.
evidence_strength: Moderate: DanceTrack (peer-reviewed [uncertain venue], public data/code, clear Table 4 and oracle Table 2) and Siam R-CNN/KeepTrack (peer-reviewed, code) are solid; SAMURAI is a preprint with single-run ablations and minor table/text inconsistencies (best Kalman weight 0.15 in table vs 0.2 in text). No independent replications checked; no confidence intervals in any source.
where_distinction_is_made: Not applicable as a single mechanism. Observed across sources: separating the right object from similar ones by per-frame appearance/quality scores fails (DanceTrack appearance, SAM2 affinity); sources that succeed move the distinction into motion/geometry consistency (DanceTrack motion models, SAMURAI Kalman re-scoring) or into history-based identity (KeepTrack, Siam R-CNN TDPA).
feature_dependence: The counterexamples concern rich RGB appearance (re-ID CNN in DeepSORT, SAM2 Hiera features) failing among look-alike objects; this makes it unlikely that weaker FlyVis features succeed via appearance alone; motion consistency is the cue that held up. No source tested small temporal motion features as identity cues.
association_consequence: DanceTrack directly measures association: appearance added to Kalman/IoU association lowered HOTA by 2.0 and IDF1 by 1.5 (Table 4). For our stand this means an external IoU/Kalman guard is a strong no-fly control and could deliver the same identity-preservation effect as a FlyVis correction; a FlyVis correction that conflicts with the IoU-consistent match (as in our R1 case, cost 0.123 -> 1.0) is the failure mode to expect.
difference_from_tried: No new mechanism to try; this screening explains and supports our negative results: z13_candidate_identity_v1 (identity via appearance+distance worse than top1, not better than geometry) matches the DanceTrack pattern; z13_absolute_confidence_v1 (raw response height did not select useful centres) matches the SAM2 'affinity not robust' observation; z13_observed_memory_v1 / z13_query_memory_v1 (memory did not help) match the weak-appearance regime. It is a source of explanation, not a reason to repeat any of these experiments.
memory_write_policy: Not applicable (screening). SAMURAI writes a frame to memory only if mask affinity, object presence and Kalman motion scores pass thresholds; ablation shows the gate helps on average (+4.35 AUC) but not under illumination variation (LaSOText IV -2.2 to -2.4 AUC).
distractor_representation: Not applicable (screening). DanceTrack trackers: other objects are separate tracks; SAMURAI: implicit (multiple mask hypotheses re-scored); Siam R-CNN/KeepTrack: explicit tracklets/candidate ids.
refusal_evidence_horizon: Not applicable (screening). Note: the per-frame quality score (SAM2) is the basis criticised; history-based schemes (KeepTrack, Siam R-CNN) accumulate over frames.
loss_on_applied_decision: Not applicable (screening); in none of the cited counterexamples is the loss defined on the applied association decision.
association_entry_point: DanceTrack: appearance enters the matching cost (DeepSORT) - and hurts there. SAMURAI: candidate mask selection and memory write. Others: not applicable.
no_fly_control_equivalent: IoU-only and Kalman-gated association (DanceTrack Tables 2, 4, 5 show these are the strongest when appearance is uniform); OC-SORT-style motion association; SAMURAI-style Kalman re-scoring of candidates without FlyVis. These should be the mandatory no-fly controls for any FlyVis correction.
hard_subset_evaluation: DanceTrack itself is the hard set (selected by design: uniform appearance, diverse motion; quantified by lower re-ID cosine distance than MOT17 and lower adjacent-frame IoU). SAMURAI reports LaSOText attributes (illumination variation, deformation). No DiDi or MOSE-PTS evaluation in these sources.
temporal_information_availability: All cited mechanisms are online and causal (current + past frames, zero added latency): SORT/DeepSORT/OC-SORT, SAMURAI, Siam R-CNN TDPA, KeepTrack. No future-frame selection involved, so the negative effects are those an online tracker would experience.
depth_level: Short screening, as set in the item. Should not move to full analysis: it provides cautions and control requirements rather than a mechanism to implement. A targeted follow-up (in N14/N16) could look for 2023-2026 negative ablations on DiDi/MOSE (distractor-aware memory failing) if the synthesis needs them.
